cards.explanation: The stone has been removed. Mary gets to the tomb while it's still dark, and the stone is no longer at the entrance (John 20:1). That's the first thing that tells her something is off. Imagine walking up to your own front door in the dark and the door is just GONE. Friends, I think she stopped dead in her tracks.

The answer is False. Mary doesn't know where the Lord's body has been put. She says, "They have taken the Lord out of the tomb, and we do not know where they have put Him!" (John 20:2). She's missing the answer, and she runs to tell Peter and the other disciple anyway. Ever sprint to tell somebody a problem you can't solve yet? That's Mary.

The other disciple gets to the tomb first. John 20:4 says the two were running together, but the other disciple outran Peter and reached the tomb first. No trophy is mentioned, friends, but I'd print one. I'd just hop slowly toward it.

The answer is True. The other disciple bends down and looks in at the linen cloths lying there, but he does not go in (John 20:5). He stops at the door and peeks. Friends, we've ALL done the careful peek before the big step.

The answer is head. John 20:7 says the cloth that had been around Jesus' head was rolled up, lying separate from the linen cloths. It's a small detail, but the writer thought it was worth including. I think Peter noticed that cloth sitting off by itself.
He believes. John 20:8 says the other disciple "…saw and believed." He sees the tomb for himself, and belief follows. Notice, friends, the verse stops there and doesn't spell out more.

The answer is False. John 20:9 says, "For they still did not understand from the Scripture that Jesus had to rise from the dead." They're standing at an empty tomb and the full picture hasn't clicked. I've read the instructions on a cookie box three times and still missed the point, so no judgment from me.

She sees two angels in white. John 20:12 says she saw them sitting where the body of Jesus had lain, one at the head and the other at the feet. She came looking for a body and found two angels. Bet that was NOT on her list, friends.

The word is sitting. John 20:12 says the two angels in white were sitting where the body of Jesus had lain, one at the head and the other at the feet. Mary had bent down to look into the tomb when she saw them. Sitting in that spot is quiet, and nothing in the verse says they were doing anything else.

She tells them someone has taken her Lord away. Mary says, "Because they have taken my Lord away, and I do not know where they have put Him" (John 20:13). She doesn't know where He is, and that's what has her weeping. I think, friends, she has one thing on her mind.

The answer is False. Mary sees Him standing there, but John 20:14 says she "…did not recognize that it was Jesus." She looks right at Him and doesn't know Him yet. The text doesn't say why, so I'll leave that open.

The word is gardener. John 20:15 says Mary was "Thinking He was the gardener…" So she asks Him where the body has been put. She doesn't recognize Him yet (John 20:14), and a man standing there is who she takes Him to be.
Jesus says her name, and that's all it takes. He says, "Mary" (John 20:16). One word, and she turns. I've had my name called across a bakery before, friends, but never like THAT.
Jesus sends her to go and tell His brothers. He says, "But go and tell My brothers…" (John 20:17). He gives her a message to carry. She's sent, and she goes.

The answer is True. Jesus tells Mary to go and tell His brothers, "I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God." (John 20:17). He's giving her a message to carry to them. She's the one trusted to deliver it.

She tells them she has seen the Lord. Mary announces to the disciples, "I have seen the Lord!" (John 20:18). And she tells them what He had said to her. She started the morning weeping, friends, and now she's got news.
